title: More pulsation terms reduce sum-tone errors by 35 to 37 percent in 14 Kepler quarters of KIC 10001893
abstract: We test whether added pulsation terms improve a sum-tone test for KIC 10001893. An instantaneous quadratic response to two fixed parent modes requires equal intrinsic sum and difference amplitudes. We reuse 14 Kepler release-25 long-cadence quarters and published quarter-specific frequency lists. With up to 40 selected extra entries, the main sum-amplitude error radii fall by 35 to 37 percent, from 68 to 85 ppm to 45 to 54 ppm. Sum and difference amplitude intervals still overlap in all 96 dependent settings. At least 90.7 percent of joint signal design information remains. Thus added pulsation terms improve conditional precision but do not reject the restricted stellar explanation. Same-data frequency selection, source mixing, aliases and estimated block covariance limit the result. No new signal or planet is confirmed. Code, aggregate fits, source hashes and external retrieval steps are included.
